fields.sample_size: 91 household questionnaires in six purposively and conveniently selected villages (Tshirolwe Ext2 9, Mabirimisa 11, Tshithunitshanntha 26, Tshirolwe 15, Tshithuni 15, Mapakhopele 15) of Makhado Biaba Town (about 6,000 residents, nine villages); interviews with municipal officials; land-use mapping 1990-2020
fields.effect_estimate: Municipal services (water, electricity, sewerage, refuse collection) are available in the peri-urban villages despite distance from the core, but unevenly: new settlements leapfrog onto vacant unserviced land faster than the municipality extends infrastructure; the study also reports ecosystem-service losses from land-use change. Descriptive mixed-methods case study; not an evaluation of a legal measure.
fields.study_design: exploratory mixed-methods case study (land-use mapping, 91-household questionnaire, municipal official interviews; one small town)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (study area, six villages, 91 questionnaires); Results; Discussion
fields.exact_location: Methods (study area, six villages, 91 questionnaires); Results; Discussion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: an exploratory mixed-methods case study of peri-urban expansion in Makhado Biaba, Limpopo (91 household questionnaires in six villages, municipal interviews, land-use mapping 1990-2020), read in full text 2026-10-04. Services are present but unevenly extended; leapfrog settlement outpaces infrastructure.
